ref_atoms.ref_content: UART smoke test with few bytes transmitted and received asynchronously and in parallel with scoreboard checks. TX and RX have 2 independent threads respectively: program one Tx item in register and wait for it to complete at uart interface, before send another one; sequencally send one Rx byte, then immediately read from register and check it.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes explicit UART TX/RX operations: programming a Tx item in a register, waiting for interface completion, and sequentially reading back a received byte, targeting concrete hardware behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Basic sequence that is extended by most of random sequence. TX and RX have 2 independent threads respectively. TX: keep programming csr wdata with random delay when fifo isn't full. RX: 2 processes. One is to send item through uart interface when fifo isn't full and the other is to read csr rdata when fifo isn't empty.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specifies TX/RX thread interactions with explicit CSR signals (wdata, rdata) and fifo-full/empty conditions, forming a concrete verification scenario.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Send / receive bytes with parity and odd parity enabled randomly.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Directly tests the UART parity hardware feature with random enabling of odd parity, a specific configurable mechanism.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Enable parity and randomly set even/odd parity. Inject parity error randomly on data sent from rx and ensure the interrupt is raised.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies parity error injection and the associated interrupt assertion, targeting a precise error detection mechanism.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Program random tx/rx fifo watermark level and keep sending random tx/rx data to fifo. As the number of pending data entries in the tx/rx fifo reaches the programmed watermark level (fifo size >= watermark level), ensure that the watermark interrupt is asserted. Ensure interrupt stays asserted until cleared as well as fifo level dropped. The tx/rx watermark interrupt is sticky.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the programmable watermark level and the sticky watermark interrupt, a concrete hardware feature with detailed assertion/deassertion behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Send over 32 bytes of data but stop when fifo is full.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Targets the specific fifo full condition and its effect on data flow, a well-defined hardware boundary case.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Keep sending over 32 bytes of data over tx/rx fifo. Ensure excess data bytes are dropped and check overflow interrupt. This uart_fifo_overflow_vseq is extent from uart_fifo_full_vseq and override the constraint to be able to send data over fifo size.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Explicitly tests the overflow condition, dropping of excess data, and the overflow interrupt, a specific error-handling mechanism.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Fill up the tx/rx fifo. After a random number of bytes shows up on fifo, reset the fifo and ensure that the remaining data bytes do not show up. This sequence is extent from uart_fifo_overflow_vseq, so it can also reset when fifo is at any level, including full or overflow.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Tests the fifo reset behavior at various levels, verifying that pending data is discarded, a precise hardware reset scenario.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Inject frame error in parity and non-parity cases by not setting stop bit = 1. Ensure the interrupt gets asserted.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Targets frame error injection via stop bit violation and the resulting interrupt, a specific error detection path.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Program random number of break detection characters. Create a frame error scenario and send random number of 0 bytes. If that random number exceeds the programmed break characters, ensure that the break_err interrupt is asserted.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies the break detection mechanism with a programmable threshold and the break_err interrupt, a concrete error condition.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Program timeout_ctrl register to randomize the timeout. Send random number of data over rx. Wait until it's about to timeout, then check timeout interrupt doesn't fire. Wait for timeout and check timeout interrupt fires. Wait until it's about to timeout, then use either read csr rdata or send RX item through uart interface to reset timeout timer in order to ensure timeout never fires.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes detailed timeout control register programming, interrupt assertion/suppression, and timer reset via CSR read or RX activity, a precise hardware mechanism.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Run fifo_full_vseq with very small delays.
Enable system looback, then drive uart TX and data will be loopbacked through RX. After loopback is done, uart.RDATA will be equal to the data programmed to uart.WDATA.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Tests the system loopback path with explicit data comparison between uart.TX/RX and the WDAT/RDATA registers, a specific hardware data path.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Enable line loopback and drive uart_rx with random data and random delay. Check uart_tx has same value as uart_rx. There is not synchronizer register between uart_rx and uart_tx during line loopback.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies the line loopback mode where uart_rx directly drives uart_tx without a synchronizer, a specific hardware connection.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Use 16x fast clk to sample it, data on uart_rx need to be stable for 3 clocks, otherwise, data change won't be taken. Enable noise filter and drive many glitches. Each glitch doesn't lasts less than 3 clocks. Ensure the noise will be filterred out and it doesn't affect next normal transaction.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Targets the noise filter with a precise 16x fast clock sampling and 3-clock stability requirement, describing glitch rejection behavior.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Start bit should last for at least half baud clock, otherwise, it will be dropped. It's always enabled. Drive start bit for less than half cycle. Ensure the start bit will be dropped.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes the always-on start bit filter with a half-baud-clock duration requirement, a specific hardware filter rule.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Enable override control and use register programming to drive uart output directly.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Tests the override control feature that allows direct register-driven manipulation of the UART output, a specific alternate control path.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Use 16x baud clock to sample uart rx. Drive uart rx with 16 bits value, using 16x baud clock. Read RX oversampled value and ensure it's same as driven value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Verifies the RX oversampling mechanism with a 16x baud clock, comparing the captured oversampled value against the driven bit pattern.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Reduce delay to fill TX fifo and read RX fifo to ensure back2back transfers. Use long back2back transfer to ensure clock difference won't be accumulated across transactions. Uart monitor checks the clock offset between sender and receiver is never over 1/4 of the period.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes back-to-back transfer stress with a monitor that checks clock offset < 1/4 period, targeting timing integrity across continuous transfers.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Combine above sequences in one test to run sequentially, except csr sequence and uart_rx_oversample_vseq (requires zero_delays). Randomly add reset between each sequence.
